title: Building AETHER with AI: a browser-based multiplayer space exploration game
author: Competitive-Hornet17
selftext:
I’m building AETHER, a multiplayer space exploration game that runs entirely in the browser. It isn’t public yet.



The project is being developed heavily with AI. My goal is to use AI for continuous iteration on mechanics and systems, rather than treating the game as ever truly “finished”. I’m especially interested in how AI-assisted development can stay coherent instead of turning into shallow feature accumulation.



The current prototype includes:



\- huge procedural space

\- 6DoF ship flight

\- warp / interstellar travel

\- planets you can approach and enter

\- atmospheric re-entry

\- manual 2D VTOL landing with gravity

\- 2D planetary exploration

\- mining, caves and resources

\- EVA in space

\- explorable ship interiors

\- repair systems

\- multiplayer encounters

\- SOS / ship towing

\- procedural discoveries and a Galactic Codex



Early video footage:

[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Xl2LBLNNizE](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Xl2LBLNNizE)



Two questions:



1. Would you play something like this?

2. Would you be interested in helping shape the game through feature ideas, prompts, or even implementations that could become part of the project?



I’d also be interested in hearing from other developers using AI: how do you keep a long-running AI-assisted project focused and consistent?
